offence_severity: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and also liable to fine for Section 498A; imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than five years and fine not less than fifteen thousand rupees or the value of the dowry for Section 3 of the Dowry Act; imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months, but which may extend to two years and fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees for Section 4 of the Dowry Act
number_of_offences: Charges under Sections 498A of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Act; chargesheet and trial pending against the appellants
motive: Retaliatory measure intended to settle scores with appellant No.1 and his family members
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the FIR lodged by respondent No.2 was initiated with ulterior motives to settle personal scores and grudges against appellant No.1 and his family members, and that the allegations were vague, omnibus, and not believable.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses, particularly respondent No.2, as having made allegations motivated by retribution rather than legitimate grievances, and found the allegations against the appellants to be vague and not supported by concrete evidence.
trial_duration: FIR lodged on 01.02.2022, chargesheet filed on 03.06.2022, trial pending in the Court of 1st Additional Junior Civil Judge-cum-Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Malkajgiri
legal_representation: Shubham Kumar, Anubhav Jain, Ms. Nayan Saini, Dhruv Goyal, Ms. Honey Verma, Rahul Mohod, Sanjay Gyan, Dr. Varnit Sharma, Chand Qureshi, Advs. for the Petitioners; Ms. Devina Sehgal, S Uday Bhanu, Advs. for the Respondents

appeal_history.trial_court: High Court refused to quash the criminal proceedings
appeal_history.high_court: High Court refused to quash the criminal proceedings
appeal_history.supreme_court: Supreme Court quashed the FIR, chargesheet and trial pending against the appellants

prosecution_argument: The State argued that a prima facie case was made out against the appellants for harassing respondent No.2 and demanding dowry from her, citing the FIR and the father of respondent No.2's testimony.
defence_argument: The appellants' counsel submitted that the FIR was a retaliatory measure intended to settle scores with appellant No.1 and his family members, with vague and omnibus allegations against the family members, and that the allegations were not specific or supported by concrete evidence.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the parameters outlined in the Bhajan Lal case to determine whether the FIR should be quashed, focusing on the presence of mala fide and ulterior motives in initiating the criminal proceedings.
precedent_relied_upon: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal [1990] Supp. 3 SCR 259 : (1992) Supp. 1 SCC 335; G.V. Rao v. L.H.V. Prasad [2000] 2 SCR 123 : (2000) 3 SCC 693; Preeti Gupta v. State of Jharkhand [2010] 9 SCR 1168 : (2010) 7 SCC 667
